reserveReview.rationale: The 2026-07-14 review recorded a Moneta 80% money-market-fund and 20% USD bank-deposit disclosure. It did not establish a combined-token portfolio across both issuers. The NBX whitepaper notified 2026-09-24 expressly establishes separate, non-cross-backed reserve books and issuer-attributed redemption obligations. Historical composition and review dates are retained without presenting the older allocation as a current whole-asset measurement.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Historical Moneta-only allocation disclosure; no current matched combined-token portfolio across the separate issuer books
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The 2026-09-24 NBX whitepaper expressly separates Moneta and NBX reserve books and liabilities with no pooled or cross-backed reserve. The historical Moneta 80/20 allocation is not a current combined-token composition; current issuer-attributed reserve values, provider allocations and a matched whole-asset liability denominator remain unestablished.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: The earlier sources establish separate reserve pools, segregated accounts and no rehypothecation for Moneta's reserve. The NBX whitepaper notified 2026-09-24 additionally describes NBX-specific creditor protection, recovery/redemption plans and continuing NBX-funded redemption if Moneta mint/burn cooperation fails. Those protections do not extend to Moneta-attributable issuance: its NBX redemption requires settled Moneta funds, and unresolved issuer attribution can delay processing. Current provider shares and matched issuer-book liabilities remain unestablished; no whole-token statutory bankruptcy-remoteness or composition refresh is inferred.
